div.head: Duns 8.1
div.ab: Se ðe hit him to teo, sylle sixa sum ðone að, þæt he hit him swa to teo, swa hit him ðeofstolen wære.
Qui sibi repetit, det sex sol. iusiurandum, quod ita sibi attrahat, sicut ei furatum fuit.
He who would claim the cattle [the accuser] must swear (as one of six) the oath: that he makes the claim [for the cattle] just as if they had been stolen by thieves.
Jener [Anefänger], der es für sich beansprucht, leiste als einer von sechs [d. h. mit fünf Helfern] folgenden Eid: ‘dass er es so für sich beanspruche, wie es ihm von Dieben gestohlen worden sei’.
Let [the attacher] who claims it for himself give, as one of six [i.e. with five helpers], the following oath: ‘that he claims it for himself just as it was stolen from him by thieves’.
div.note: MS R of the Quadripartitus reads ‘sex solidorum’, which Liebermann thinks corrupted from ‘se sexto’. Liebermann compares VI As 9 and Swer 2.
